name: Cellular radio technology (4G, 5G)
plain: Reads whether the phone is on LTE, 5G or 3G.
meaning: Shows connection quality and device capability; low sensitivity.

android.note: API 30 added READ_PHONE_STATE requirement; ConnectivityManager gives transport without it

limits.headline: Can tell if you are on 3G, 4G or 5G, with a prompt on Android
limits.user_action: You tap Allow for Phone or Phone state on Android; iPhone shows nothing
can: See whether the phone is on 3G, 4G LTE or 5G
Check each SIM on iPhone with dual SIM
cannot: Get the exact radio type on Android 11 and newer without Phone state permission
See your calls or number from the radio type
Learn more than Wi-Fi or cellular from Android connection info alone
limits.differs: Android 11 and newer needs Phone state permission for the exact type. iPhone shares it without a prompt, per SIM.

story.what_it_is: An app can see whether your phone is on 3G, 4G or 5G.
story.for_you: You do not see it. A video app may pick a sharper picture on 5G and a lighter one on 3G. It tells the app how fast and how new your connection and phone are.
story.for_makers: Makers tune streaming and downloads to how good the link is. It is a low risk bit. It also hints at the phone model and your place, because 5G exists only in some areas.

use_cases.example: A video app starts at a high quality on 5G and drops quickly on a slow 3G link.
A cloud gaming app warns you that 4G is too slow and suggests Wi-Fi.
A live video app lowers the picture while you walk into an area with a weaker signal.
A map app downloads offline map areas faster when it sees 5G.
A network quality tool collects radio types to map where 5G works in a city.
A carrier ad service targets 5G users with new phone deals.

story.android_note: Android apps read the radio technology with a phone state permission on newer versions.
story.ios_note: iPhone apps get a coarse label through the telephony network info, and details are limited.
